_meta.note: Regression reference for Micro-Adventure Mapper, re-recorded after the 2026-09-03 grounding rewrite. The v1 golden was discarded: its expected output contained time_start/time_end clock fields, a street-address `location` field, `pro_tip`, `why_adventure`, `difficulty`, `transit_between`, `rainy_backup` and `extend_it` — every one of which the new schema either renamed or removed. Re-run with `npm run check:golden micro-adventure-mapper` against a local backend and diff for QUALITY, not exact match. What check-golden cannot see, and what actually matters here: (1) no clock time, address, cross street, price, opening hour or admission claim anywhere; (2) no claim about who goes to a place, how busy it is, whether doors are open, or what staff will do; (3) a named venue only where broadly stable — otherwise a described place TYPE plus a `verify` line; (4) the outing fits the supplied time WITHOUT padding to fill it, so one hour may legitimately be one stop. Each case carries its own `guards` line. See audit/tool-notes/MICROADVENTUREMAPPER-NOTES.md.

cases.name: generate-two-hours-art-walk
cases.guards: The case the 2026-09-03 rewrite exists for — the same input produced 'Pilsen is where Chicago's street art scene actually lives', 'work most tourists miss', 'afternoon light hits murals better between 2-4 PM', 'many have open doors on weekends' and 'if a door is propped open, you're welcome to look'. NONE of that may return. No clock times anywhere (the schema has no time_start/time_end). No street address or cross street (the schema has area, not location). No claim about who goes somewhere, how busy it is, whether doors are open, or what staff will do. Named venues only where broadly stable; otherwise a described place TYPE. Every stop that depends on something current carries a `verify` line.  Plus the 2026-09-03 final pass: no companion type turned into a personal preference ('lets you linger where history interests you most'), no physical state the itinerary supposedly causes ('walked enough to be genuinely hungry', 'rest your feet'), no ornamental history ('a gathering space since the 1600s', 'built in 1723'), no statement of what a place currently sells or serves ('Faneuil Hall has vendors and casual spots', 'areas with independent cafes'), no admission claim ('many have free or low-cost admission'), no distance more precise than it can know ('a 2.4-mile route'), and no neighbourhood appended to a place name in parentheses — Old North Church is not in Beacon Hill, and a broad accurate area label beats a precise wrong one. `verify` should be EMPTY on most stops: walking a public route does not depend on whether every site along it is open, and an over-broad chore trains people to skip the ones that matter.

adventure.name: Pilsen Mural Walk
adventure.tagline: Two hours exploring street art and independent galleries on foot.
adventure.why_this_fits: Pilsen is known for public murals and galleries accessible by walking, which works well for a solo outing at your own pace with photography and art as interests. The low budget fits since street art and many galleries are free to view.

stops.name: Pilsen commercial district murals
stops.description: Walk the main commercial blocks looking for public murals and street art. Stop wherever a piece catches your eye to photograph and study the work. Pilsen has significant public art, but specific current murals change—your maps app can help you locate 'Pilsen murals' or 'Chicago street art' to see what's documented as currently visible. Move at your own pace; there is no destination, only direction.
stops.small_twist: Photograph the same mural from at least two different angles or times of day if the light shifts while you walk.
stops.photo_op: Murals are the main draw; look for compositions with strong light, interesting angles, or details that reward close focus.

stops.name: Independent gallery or arts space
stops.description: Use your maps app to locate an independent gallery, artist studio, or arts nonprofit within walking distance of where you are. Many are free to enter and open to foot traffic. Step inside, spend time with the work, and ask yourself what drew you to it. If the door is closed or the space is not open to visitors, this is a natural point to turn back or explore a different block.
stops.small_twist: If the gallery has work by a local artist, look for something you would not expect to see—a technique, subject, or material that surprises you.
stops.verify: Current gallery hours and whether walk-in visitors are welcome. Check before entering or use a closed door as a signal to explore the surrounding blocks instead.

between_stops.guidance: Continue walking through the neighborhood. Choose a gallery or arts space that is within reasonable walking distance of where you end the first stop.

backup_plan.when_to_use: If weather makes outdoor photography uncomfortable or if you want to move indoors before the 2 hours are done
backup_plan.description: Use your maps app to find an open museum, cultural center, or independent bookstore in Pilsen. Many host art and photography and welcome walk-ins. Spend the remaining time indoors with work you can study closely.

keep_going.suggestion: If you still have time, pick one street or block you liked and walk it again more slowly, or use your maps app to find a cafe or small independent shop nearby to sit and review the photos you took.

cases.name: generate-one-hour-free-accessible
cases.guards: One hour, free-only, transit, family, wheelchair. One hour may justify only 1-2 stops — a forced 3-5 is the failure this catches. `free` is a hard budget constraint, so no cost may imply spending. Accessibility is a hard constraint: nothing may be CALLED accessible, and anything that depends on current local conditions belongs in `verify`. Photography is not among the interests, so a photo_op is allowed only where the scene naturally supports it.  Plus the 2026-09-03 final pass: no companion type turned into a personal preference ('lets you linger where history interests you most'), no physical state the itinerary supposedly causes ('walked enough to be genuinely hungry', 'rest your feet'), no ornamental history ('a gathering space since the 1600s', 'built in 1723'), no statement of what a place currently sells or serves ('Faneuil Hall has vendors and casual spots', 'areas with independent cafes'), no admission claim ('many have free or low-cost admission'), no distance more precise than it can know ('a 2.4-mile route'), and no neighbourhood appended to a place name in parentheses — Old North Church is not in Beacon Hill, and a broad accurate area label beats a precise wrong one. `verify` should be EMPTY on most stops: walking a public route does not depend on whether every site along it is open, and an over-broad chore trains people to skip the ones that matter.

adventure.name: Evening Market Wander & Taste
adventure.tagline: A slow evening walk through a public market with free sampling and low-key people-watching.
adventure.why_this_fits: Public markets in Porto are accessible, moving slowly suits a chill vibe with kids, transit gets you there, and market stalls often offer free tastes without obligation to buy. One straightforward stop fits your hour without rushing.

stops.name: A public market in central Porto
stops.description: Walk slowly through the market, watch vendors, ask about samples (many offer them freely), notice what foods are local or unfamiliar, and let the kids explore at their own pace. No purchase needed — the point is presence and discovery. Wheelchair users should verify accessibility of specific market entrance and main aisles before visiting.
stops.small_twist: Ask one vendor a genuine question about something you don't recognize — how it is used, where it comes from, or what it tastes like. Most people enjoy sharing.
stops.verify: Confirm the market is open this evening and has accessible entry/main aisles for wheelchair access.

what_to_bring: Transit card or payment for fares
Small bag for any unexpected finds

backup_plan.when_to_use: If the market is closed or inaccessible this evening, or if the vibe feels too crowded for a chill outing with kids
backup_plan.description: Use your maps app to find an open public space in central Porto — a plaza, waterfront area, or park — where you can sit and watch the evening. Stop for street food or a casual vendor spot if you find one that appeals, or stay free and simply observe. The same slow-walking, low-key food discovery works in a different setting.

keep_going.suggestion: If energy and time allow, take transit to a waterfront viewpoint or public plaza in central Porto and sit while evening light changes. This extends the chill vibe without adding structure.

cases.name: regenerate-different-outing
cases.guards: Same constraints, a different outing. It must differ in at least two of activity, area, pace, stop type or theme — but must NOT switch away from the vibe the visitor selected. Same grounding rules as generate.  Plus the 2026-09-03 final pass: no companion type turned into a personal preference ('lets you linger where history interests you most'), no physical state the itinerary supposedly causes ('walked enough to be genuinely hungry', 'rest your feet'), no ornamental history ('a gathering space since the 1600s', 'built in 1723'), no statement of what a place currently sells or serves ('Faneuil Hall has vendors and casual spots', 'areas with independent cafes'), no admission claim ('many have free or low-cost admission'), no distance more precise than it can know ('a 2.4-mile route'), and no neighbourhood appended to a place name in parentheses — Old North Church is not in Beacon Hill, and a broad accurate area label beats a precise wrong one. `verify` should be EMPTY on most stops: walking a public route does not depend on whether every site along it is open, and an over-broad chore trains people to skip the ones that matter.

adventure.name: Pilsen Gallery Crawl & Street Detail Hunt
adventure.tagline: Move slowly through galleries and side streets, hunting for visual details that reward close attention.
adventure.why_this_fits: A slower-paced alternative to the mural walk that keeps photography as the active task but shifts focus from standoff murals to indoor gallery work and found details on side streets. The pace works for solo exploration at your own rhythm, and galleries are free or low-cost in Pilsen.

stops.name: Pilsen gallery district
stops.description: Pick one or two smaller galleries to move through deliberately. Rather than aiming to see everything, spend time on individual pieces — composition, materials, what the work is asking you to look at. This is different work than photographing the obvious thing. If a gallery has a back room or upstairs, go there.
stops.small_twist: Challenge yourself to find one piece in each gallery that would be hard to photograph well, and spend a moment understanding why.
stops.photo_op: Work you see inside, if the gallery permits photography — ask first. Many contemporary galleries do.
stops.verify: Which galleries are open right now — search your maps app for 'galleries Pilsen Chicago' and check hours before entering.

stops.name: Side streets and architectural details
stops.description: Walk the quieter blocks between the main gallery and commercial streets. Look for: brick textures, fire escapes, window frames, small hand-painted signs, peeling paint that forms accidental colors, reflections in glass, how light hits a corner at this hour. The point is to see what you walked past before. Stop when something catches your eye and look at it for a minute.
stops.small_twist: Try photographing the same subject (a door, a wall, a window) from three different distances or angles. Notice what changes about how you see it.
stops.photo_op: Details, textures, light, reflections — the unglamorous visual stuff that exists everywhere if you look.

between_stops.guidance: Exit the gallery district and walk toward one of the quieter residential blocks nearby. You'll shift from curated interiors to the street itself.

backup_plan.when_to_use: If the galleries you planned to visit are closed or too crowded, or if you want to move indoors for any reason
backup_plan.description: Use your maps app to find an open library or museum with current exhibits in or near Pilsen. Many have free hours or low admission. Alternatively, look for a used bookstore or vintage shop in the area — these often have visual richness worth photographing, and the browsing pace matches a solo visit.

keep_going.suggestion: If you still have time and energy, move into one of the adjacent residential blocks you have not explored yet and continue the detail hunt. The visual reward of that kind of work deepens the longer you stay with it. Alternatively, find a casual coffee spot or cafe along your route and review the photos you took — this helps you see what you were drawn to and what worked photographically.

cases.name: swap-stop-one
cases.guards: Returns ONE stop and ONE transition — `{stop, transition}`, not the arrays the old version returned, which the frontend merges by number. The replacement must preserve the theme, fit roughly the same time, respect the transport, and carry no invented address, price, opening hour or exact travel time. If no current venue can safely be named, a described place type plus a `verify` line is the correct answer. stop.name: Artist studio or workspace open to visitors
stop.description: Pilsen has a working artist community, and some studios and shared creative spaces periodically open their doors or maintain visiting hours. Use your maps app to search 'Pilsen artist studio' or 'open studio Chicago' to find current options. When you find one that is open, spend time observing the work in progress, talking with artists if they are available, and photographing pieces that interest you. If no studio is currently open to visitors, use this time to explore the surrounding blocks on foot—look for storefronts with artist signage, community bulletin boards, or visible creative work that signals where local makers work.
stop.small_twist: Ask an artist on-site (if present) about one piece—what drew them to that subject or technique. Photograph both the finished work and any materials or process visible in the space.
stop.verify: Before heading out, check your maps app for 'Pilsen artist studio,' 'open studio,' or 'artist workspace visitor hours' to confirm a space is accessible when you plan to visit.

transition.guidance: Walk toward the second stop (the independent gallery or arts space you selected) using your maps app for routing.
transition.estimated_time: About 10–15 minutes walking, depending on which studio you visit and where the gallery is located.
